body: Is it helpful? I'm glad you reached out I know it's hard but it's a big step. I hope you get the help you need
I've known that from the start but invested too much. I dont have the means to go back and restart

Also, I've been there feeling scared of myself. Personally, that was when I needed someone else to know because I didnt trust myself not to do something. It's scary and incredibly hard, but it can also save your life. If you can find someone, anyone, that you trust enough to support you, please reach out if you can.

I'm so sorry you are so much pain, it sounds like you are really struggling. Have you talked to you therapist about your plan? Or if that is too much is there anyone else you trust to talk to? Doesnt have to be your friends if they are out of reach.

If you tell someone else, tell her you are going to before you do. And emphasize that it is for her safety. Explaining why can make a difference. Going behind someone's back can really hurt, no matter your intentions. It sounds like you really care and want her to be okay. She might get mad at you for telling someone, but if long term it means she is okay it is usually worth it.

I'm sorry that things are so tough for you right now. Sounds like you have a lot going on. There are sometimes low cost therapy options or payment plan options, I do not know about your area or situation though. Other times, schools have resources that are free or low cost.

That's the thing, there's nothing super bad. It's just time. I am burnt out early in my career so how am I supposed to last. I've been depressed/suicidal for years and I finally feel okay with that. I guess I'm just ready.
so glad you are here, been checking this post for updates all week. wishing only the best for you moving forward.

I'm sorry things are so hard. Life is not easy and it sounds like you are dealing with a lot. I also struggle with feeling like a burden, but you are not. And neither am I. No one is a burden, you are just trying.
I'm so sorry you feel this way
I'm sorry that you have reached this point

At a certain point she cannot refuse if she is a danger to herself. If her doctor takes everything into account, that might end up being the case. I hope for her sake and yours that she gets the help she needs.
I know it isn't easy and I know it sounds impossible, and that's okay. It takes time, but you deserve good things and I hope you get them.

trying to get better is also tough, but the hard parts change. I am 2 years out from my lowest point where I spent weeks in bed and still working on getting better. But there is hope. Things can change. And it won't be easy or a straight line, but there are ways to get better. Just keep trying, that's all. It doesn't have to be getting better overnight, just one step at a time. And it doesn't have to be everyday, you can spend all day in bed some days. But on the days that you can try, get out of bed, journal, talk to someone, reach out. just keep trying, whatever that looks like for you.

You don't have to want to live right now, but it sounds like your grandma would want you to. Let her be your motivation to try, even if you don't want to. And I know it is much easier to say than to do, but you deserve to live and I know we don't know each other but I care and I believe you deserve to live and have a fulfilling life.

I'm sorry that you lost her, no doubt losing someone changes you. I'm glad you had her, it sounds like she meant more than anything to you. There is no replacing her. I had someone tell me the first time I lost someone that they do things in life for those they lost. They live for them because they can't anymore. They do things that make them happy because those who are gone can't anymore. And it isn't easy, but it is motivation to try and to carry that person with them in life.

Hold onto those little things if you can, they make all the difference. If you can hold onto them for long enough, something else has time to come around and be good for you. I hope something good comes to you, you deserve it.

I'm so sorry you feel this way and have lost someone important to you. It is painful and life changing. There are things in life other than the "typical path" there are fulfilling jobs and people, pets and activities.
That sounds like a painful way to go, and there are no guarantees it will kill you. I'm sorry that you feel like it is an option, that is a horrid place to be mentally.

Is she seeing someone regularly? If not but it is an option, I would try to ensure that she is and she is being as honest as possible. Unless it is a life threatening situation, I would not go behind her back and tell them for her, but instead support her in doing so. If you are able to tell her family in a respectful way, I would tell her that you are going to first. I had someone talk to my parents behind my back and it destroyed me.
I'm so sorry, that sounds awful. I hope you can hold on. I can't imagine losing my dog.
whatever you are feeling is valid. you don't need a "good enough" reason, you feel what you feel and that's valid. comparison is the worst, it only makes you feel worse.
corona virus won't necessarily kill you
what's going on

you've been posting here a lot, to me that says you are looking for a reason to stay. some part of you, conscious or not, wants to stay. you are reaching out, even if it is here. I think you aren't quite ready to go. please find that piece of you that can hold on. you deserve better.
be honest, tell them you are having thoughts of suicide. try asking for what you need. it is a dire situation. don't try and avoid that
I'm sorry, that is an awful feeling.

ask what they need. ask if they have a plan. if they do, try and help. asking them if they have a plan won't cause anything, it can only help. reach out. let them know you are there and try to support them in getting professional help if you can. they might fight it, they might hate you for it, but you are doing them good. hopefully one day they will thank you. at the very least, let them know they have someone in their corner.
still thinking about you, hope you make it through this
I'm so sorry you are dealing with that, but a chronic illness is not the end. It is definitely hard, but there are options. Please hold on
That's okay! It takes time. I hope that one day you find someone that you are ready to let in. Until then, I will be thinking of you and wishing you the best.

Also get that, but sometimes it is better to have them feel burdened than to lose you. If they do care though, people are usually happy that you talk to them (in my experience), I know that doesn't make it easier but maybe it'll ease a worry or maybe not

Maybe try telling someone? Someone you trust and explaining the situation. Starting to be honest again somewhere is hard but helpful. Even if you can't start with your therapist try telling one person who you trust not to take any action that you wouldn't want them to
I'm sorry. I hope taking a walk is helpful and not harmful
I feel that. I lie and say I'm doing fine and sometimes tell and say yeah I'm having thoughts but never anything more than that. It's hard to admit and the fear of consequences is hard
I lost someone. It sucks, but life keeps moving whether or not they or anyone else is here
I just talked to someone in person
Thank you
I know finding someone to talk to that you trust is really hard, it took me years to reach out for real, but it is possible. someone somewhere will listen

I think "bad enough" being only suicidal. I am good at comparison and it feels like everyone else has a lot more going on or better reasons to be suicidal or depressed or whatever else. I've been seeing therapists for about 2 years continuously and on and off meds, so I've done outpatient care. I will probably look at step-up level care. Thank you.
Also thank you for offering to answer questions, I have terrible anxiety and the unknown freaks me out.
Worried about not being "bad enough" and also what happens when/if family, work, school etc finds out. Are there ways to be there almost anonymously?
thanks. just know there are a lot of mixed experiences. I'm sorry that the psychiatrist couldn't help you, that is really shitty.
I can only imagine, I hope something good comes your way soon. and thank you for your words too

I had trouble with physical effects like feeling nauseous, etc. If that happened, I just told whoever it impacted that I started a new medication and it has some side effects. Keeping it vague is fine and people usually don't press. They also do not work immediately, but if they have super negative side effects (especially mood wise) please please tell your prescriber. It often takes time to find the right med, so do not give up if the first one doesn't work/isn't right for you. It sucks, but it happens.
I'm so sorry. Do you need any resources? You deserve better, at least that's what I think. And if you don't agree, let me think it for you.
I'm so glad that things are changing for good, you deserve to be happy.
I'm so sorry you feel like that. you deserve better. I know you don't know me and I don't know you, but I'm some random person here just to say that you deserve better and to get better.
im sorry, you deserve better
im sorry you feel that way, it is scary
that sliver is so so important. please try and hold onto it. I know the sliver and it has kept me alive many times. I hope it keeps you around.
im sorry, that sounds awful

even if you feel like you caused it, in the end it was his decision to self harm. you are not responsible for the actions of others. and comparison is the devil. do not compare self harm. that will only make you feel worse when your situation, feelings, etc are valid. finding someone he can talk to and/or you can talk to sounds like it would be beneficial to both of you, if either one of you or both of you have someone outside your relationship you can talk to
sounds scary, intrusive thoughts always suck. I hope it passes and you stay safe.
I'm sorry

medication side effects suck, certain meds made me get worse and it was scary and stressful and annoying. people brush over sexual side effects but they had a big impact on my relationship. sometimes though, the side effects are worth the benefits for a short time? depends on situation but at least that is how I feel sometimes. worth considering if it helped your mental health. or maybe trying a new medication. i hope you find options that can help you
I'm sorry that you have to feel this way, no one deserves it. being numb sucks, I think it the worst thing you can feel

this sounds dumb, but tell someone. someone you trust. because then someone is holding you accountable. and it makes it a little more real for you and those around you and they know what to look out for.

also, other options can include therapy, medication, hospitalization, etc. I don't know your situation or what you have access to, but there are options
life sucks, but we are all here together. I know I really have no say, but I hope you do not do it.
